detail:
Dysautonomia International explains that the autonomic nervous system controls the body's automatic functions, including heart rate, blood pressure, digestion, kidney function, and temperature control. When that system malfunctions, the resulting group of conditions is called dysautonomia. The umbrella covers conditions such as POTS, vasovagal (neurocardiogenic) syncope, orthostatic hypotension, and multiple system atrophy, among others.

Symptoms vary with the form and can include lightheadedness, fainting, rapid or slow heart rate, blood pressure swings, digestive problems, abnormal sweating, and fatigue. There is no single test for the whole umbrella: evaluation usually starts with a history and orthostatic vital signs and may include tilt table testing, an autonomic reflex screen, and other tests chosen for the suspected form, while clinicians also look for underlying causes.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about evaluation for autonomic symptoms.
summary: Dysautonomia International describes dysautonomia as an umbrella term for disorders of the autonomic nervous system, the system that runs automatic functions like heart rate, blood pressure, digestion, and temperature control.
takeaways: dysautonomia is an umbrella term, not one single disease
symptoms can involve circulation, digestion, sweating, and more
evaluation often includes orthostatic vital signs and autonomic testing
talk to your doctor about which form fits your symptoms
title: Dysautonomia: when the automatic nervous system misfires
